stances.summary: American identity reflects shared cultural heroes and values
stances.quote: What Our Heroes Tell Us About America (by Rob Feld). Our shared memories expose who we really are as a nation.

stances.summary: Defends liberal establishment against anti-elite populism
stances.quote: What Locke Knew About Elites (by Teresa M. Bejan). How liberals learned to stop worrying and love the establishment.

stances.summary: Criticizes DSA as a menace
stances.quote: The DSA Is a Menace (by Garry Kasparov)

stances.summary: Institutions must enforce standards without exception
stances.quote: Surely Liberals Can Agree That Plagiarism Is Bad (by Sam Kahn). Institutions need to uphold standards. No exceptions.

stances.summary: Cautions against new DSA platform while acknowledging its appeal
stances.quote: Socialism Could Be the Future of the Democratic Party (by Charles Lane). We should reject the new DSA platform without underestimating its popular appeal.

stances.summary: Serbia faces difficult geopolitical choice between Putin and Trump
stances.quote: Serbia Turns Toward the West (by Nikola Mikovic). President Vučić is navigating a course between Putin and Trump—but will soon have to choose.

stances.summary: Germany's far-right party risks entering mainstream politics
stances.quote: This Could Be the Year Germany's Far-Right Goes Mainstream (by Katja Hoyer)

stances.summary: Questions sustainability of electoral victories over populism
stances.quote: Adam Bodnar on Why Defeating Populists at the Ballot Box Isn’t Enough. Yascha Mounk and Adam Bodnar examine why Poland’s celebrated victory over illiberalism is now very much in doubt.

stances.summary: Highlights Russia's military recruitment crisis in Ukraine war
stances.quote: Putin is Running Out of Troops (by Kathryn Stoner). As the war in Ukraine continues, Russian military recruitment is lagging.

stances.summary: Critiques Weimar comparisons; concerns about Islamist extremism in Germany
stances.quote: Katja Hoyer on Why We Should Stop Comparing Everything to Weimar. Yascha Mounk and Katja Hoyer also discuss what the Islamist attack on Berlin’s Pride parade says about the state of Germany.

stances.summary: Warns against government picking winners in business competition
stances.quote: Washington Learns the Wrong Lessons from Beijing (by Shahn Louis). The state can't just prop up the companies it wants to succeed.

stances.summary: Critiques wealth taxes as populist policy
stances.quote: Wealth Taxes Are Slopulism (by Joseph Heath)

stances.summary: Digital age severed link between economic growth and shared prosperity
stances.quote: Daron Acemoglu on Why Liberalism Became a Victim of Its Own Success. Yascha Mounk and Daron Acemoglu examine how the digital age severed the link between economic growth and shared prosperity.

stances.summary: Highlights case of educator fired for teaching assignment
stances.quote: I Taught a Short Story. My College Fired Me For It.  (by Vinita Prabhakar)

stances.summary: Sociology has abandoned empiricism for ideological conformity
stances.quote: We Must Save Sociology From Itself (by Eboo Patel). A field that once illuminated scarce truths has become an ideology in search of evidence.

stances.summary: Critiques humanitarian intervention hubris post-9/11
stances.quote: The Eras of Francis Fukuyama: How States Form. Yascha Mounk and Francis Fukuyama delve into 9/11, the hubris of humanitarian intervention, and the letter he regretted signing.

stances.summary: Local resistance strategies against authoritarian threats
stances.quote: Resistance to Authoritarianism Must Be Local (by Adam Fefer)

stances.summary: Examines Trump's expansion of executive authority and governance implications
stances.quote: On Executive Authority (by Francis Fukuyama). Francis Fukuyama explores how President Trump has tried to expand executive authority, the impact of his actions on how America will be governed in the future, and the choice facing the next U.S.

stances.summary: Warns Trump expanded executive power dangerously, difficult to reverse
stances.quote: Trump Has Revolutionized Executive Power (by Francis Fukuyama). It will take a supreme act of will for the next administration to put the genie back in the bottle.

stances.summary: Challenges left-right framing of immigration attitudes
stances.quote: What Ceuta Shows About Europe (by Ines Burrell). Why left vs right is too simplistic to explain attitudes to immigration.

stances.summary: Critiques Germany's immigration policy approach
stances.quote: Germany Has Lost the Thread on Immigration  (by Sheri Berman)

stances.summary: Opposes censorship as antisemitism remedy, defends free speech protections
stances.quote: Censorship Will Never Solve Antisemitism. Jews have always benefitted from strong protections for free speech.

stances.summary: Defends free speech victory but opposes litigation as strategy
stances.quote: J.K. Rowling Is Turning A Free Speech Victory Into A Defeat (by Jacob Mchangama). The backlash against Amnesty was justified. Suing them out of existence is not.

stances.summary: Teen social media bans miss underlying anxiety drivers in childhood
stances.quote: What a Teen Social Media Ban Overlooks (by Tim Requarth). Childhood itself has become an incubator for anxiety.

stances.summary: Argues superintelligence panic is misguided
stances.quote: The Misguided Panic About Superintelligence (by Jerry Kaplan)

stances.quote: Josh Harder on Why America Needs to Build (by Francis Fukuyama). In this conversation, recorded at the New Liberal Action Summit organized by the Center for New Liberalism in Washington, D.C., Francis Fukuyama interviews Representative Josh Harder about the obstacles to building
